PullRequest.Title: mcp: Reposition migration action
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- place the MCP migrate action inside the migratable server group
- keep the action before the not-migratable server list
- add spacing and a separator to distinguish unavailable servers as a secondary section
- cover the DOM hierarchy and ordering with a focused regression test

## Validation

- npm run transpile-client
- ESLint on the changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint on the changed CSS file
- pre-commit hygiene checks

The focused Electron test could not run in the sandbox because Electron cache access was initially denied.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the MCP migration page with migratable and unavailable servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold refresh, migration discovery must complete before the populated page renders; the diff only reparents the already-created footer during the synchronous render after candidates are available. Warm rerenders use candidates retained in customizationsByMigrationCategory and do not invoke discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the MCP migration plan by inspecting workspace MCP configuration files through the existing migration provider and file service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing cold-refresh work scales with workspace roots and MCP configuration files; it is one MCP category computation within the enabled-category refresh, not one call per rendered server row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider computation and file reads occurred before the diff; the change only relocates an existing DOM footer after discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold page population waits for this existing discovery; cached rerenders do not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and wait for the agent-host MCP support scope used to form the migration snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One support scope per MCP migration computation, independent of the number of rendered migration rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical support-scope acquisition and waiting occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold MCP migration computation waits for support discovery; the footer-positioning change is downstream and adds no IPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The rendered list scales with migratable plus unavailable MCP servers, but the added work is a single class toggle and appendChild on one footer. Existing row/list construction remains O(server count), with one MCP group and virtualized migratable rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Enabled migration categories are computed concurrently with Promise.all; MCP planning itself remains one provider request. Refreshes are sequenced/cancelled through the existing Delayer, sequence token, and disposable cancellation token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Candidate and exclusion results are retained in editor maps/arrays for warm rerenders. Context changes clear selection and candidate state; event-driven refreshes recompute discovery. The diff changes neither cache keys, invalidation, coalescing, nor negative results.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines perform only constant DOM reparenting/class updates, and traced discovery boundaries are upstream unchanged code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace-root and server counts vary, but no changed boundary or collection-scaled work was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The footer move adds bounded DOM work and does not multiply filesystem/IPC discovery or per-server rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch between the MCP page, another migration category, and the migration dashboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view synchronously restores the same footer to the migration content container before clearing and rebuilding a category page; dashboard transitions hide the existing migration surface. No external operation is required for the view switch itself.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One persistent footer node and a fixed number of category groups; restoring/reinserting the footer is constant-time regardless of candidate count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrent work is introduced. Existing section layout scheduling is coalesced to the next animation frame when a pending layout scheduler exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing candidate data and per-section scroll positions are retained across category transitions. The same footer node is reused, so transitions do not accumulate nodes or listeners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed appendChild calls target one retained node, and migrationPageDisposables are still cleared before list reconstruction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style/layout cost for a single reparent varies, but it is bounded to page rerenders rather than scroll, input, or per-row events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable repeated-work or retention issue. The reparent prevents the footer from being removed with the cleared list and does not create additional footer instances.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or scroll the MCP migration list after the action footer is placed inside the migratable group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resize schedules virtualized-section measurement/layout; scrolling remains handled by the existing scrollable element and does not execute the changed reparenting code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Layout inspects direct group children and the one virtualized MCP section. The relocated footer is counted as fixed-height content; work remains bounded by the fixed group count, not MCP server-row cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ResizeObserver notifications feed the existing animation-frame scheduler, replacing the pending scheduled layout rather than creating an unbounded queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; virtualized rows and saved section scroll positions behave as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: layoutVirtualizedSections subtracts the virtualized list height from its containing group and treats other descendants such as the footer as fixed height, while changed code runs only during page rendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser layout duration depends on pane dimensions, but the diff introduces neither per-frame geometry reads nor a resize feedback loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering or layout regression. Geometry remains handled by the existing coalesced virtualization layout.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all three changed files and traced render callers, footer lifecycle, virtualized layout, migration discovery boundaries, cache behavior, and concurrency. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
